title: Base-changed atlas covering and its canonical Cech overlap
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $f:X\to Y$ a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], $p:U\to X$ a surjective etale map from a scheme, and $v:V\to Y$ an etale map from a scheme. Schemes are viewed as algebraic spaces by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. Put $R=U\times_XU$, with projections $p_1,p_2$, and $W=V\times_YX$, $Z=V\times_YU$, $Q=V\times_YR$, using the fibre products of [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Then $R,Z,Q$ are schemes, $p_i:R\to U$, $Z\to U$, $Q\to R$, and $W\to X$ are etale, and the singleton $Z\to W$ is an etale covering. The objects $W,Z,Q$ and these covering and projection maps belong to the enlarged etale site $\mathcal C_X$ of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]. There is a canonical isomorphism $Z\times_WZ\simeq Q$ over $W$, whose two maps to $Z$ are induced by $p_1,p_2$. On a test scheme $T$, this isomorphism takes $(v_T,u_1,u_2)$, with $p u_1=p u_2$ and $f p u_i=v v_T$, to $(v_T,(u_1,u_2))$. This isomorphism commutes with all maps of etale test schemes $V'\to V$ over $Y$.

proof.text: Map the given sheaf pullback squares to presheaves. Apply representableWith_baseChange from [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence] to p and v to prove representable etaleness of p1, p2, zU, qR, wX. The scheme-test definition in [def-trf-algebraic-space], tested against the inverse of a representation of the target, gives a representing scheme for the source: the other projection is an isomorphism. Apply this successively to R, Z, Q.

proof.text: Cancel the W pullback square from Z to obtain IsPullback zU c p wX. Apply representableWith_baseChange to both the etaleness and scheme-test surjectivity of p. To turn the latter into [def-trf-algebraic-space-jointly-surjective-family], test on a field-valued section, choose a point of the surjective representing scheme, and use its residue field and residue-field morphism. Full faithfulness of Spec gives the field embedding, and the representing square gives the lifted-section equation.

proof.text: Compose representable etale maps using isEtale_comp from [def-trf-algebraic-space]; this gives chartwise etaleness of all structure maps. Identity is chartwise etale directly from its definition. Construct the six objects and eight arrows explicitly as the full subcategory of Over X in [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]. The pullback equations give their triangle identities. For the singleton presieve, its membership witnesses all have the given arrow c; reindex the residue-field lifting witness to its uncurry type to prove the covering condition.

proof.text: Cancel the Z pullback square from Q to obtain IsPullback q1 qR zU p1. Paste it with R, then cancel IsPullback c zU wX p. The result is IsPullback q1 q2 c c; the commutation follows from uniqueness of maps into W and the equations for q1 and q2. Mathlib IsPullback.isoPullback.symm gives the required canonical isomorphism and both projection identities. The full-subcategory description in [def-trf-algebraic-space] identifies its morphisms with the displayed sheaf morphisms.

proof.text: For each of q1,q2, use Z pullback uniqueness and the prescribed V and U projection equations to prove aQ followed by qi equals qi-prime followed by aZ. The projection identities of e,e-prime and d now show that both composites in the naturality square agree after qi. The Q universal property reduces equality to qV and qR; for qV use q1 followed by zV, and for qR use R uniqueness with qi followed by zU. These are equalities of sheaf maps, hence of the underlying full-subcategory morphisms of [def-trf-algebraic-space].

lean.statement: theorem space_atlas_base_change_cech_geometry {S : Scheme.{u}} (X Y : AlgebraicSpace S) (U V : Over S) (f : X ⟶ Y) (p : schemeSpace U ⟶ X) (v : schemeSpace V ⟶ Y) (hp : IsEtale p.hom.hom) (hps : IsSurjective p.hom.hom) (hv : IsEtale v.hom.hom) (R W Z Q : AlgebraicSpace S) (p₁ p₂ : R ⟶ schemeSpace U) (r : IsPullback p₁.hom p₂.hom p.hom p.hom) (wV : W ⟶ schemeSpace V) (wX : W ⟶ X) (w : IsPullback wV.hom wX.hom v.hom f.hom) (zV : Z ⟶ schemeSpace V) (zU : Z ⟶ schemeSpace U) (z : IsPullback zV.hom zU.hom v.hom (p ≫ f).hom) (qV : Q ⟶ schemeSpace V) (qR : Q ⟶ R) (q : IsPullback qV.hom qR.hom v.hom (p₁ ≫ p ≫ f).hom) (c : Z ⟶ W) (hcV : c ≫ wV = zV) (hcX : c ≫ wX = zU ≫ p) (q₁ q₂ : Q ⟶ Z) (hq₁V : q₁ ≫ zV = qV) (hq₂V : q₂ ≫ zV = qV) (hq₁U : q₁ ≫ zU = qR ≫ p₁) (hq₂U : q₂ ≫ zU = qR ≫ p₂) : (∃ T : Over S, Nonempty (R.obj.obj ≅ yoneda.obj T)) ∧ (∃ T : Over S, Nonempty (Z.obj.obj ≅ yoneda.obj T)) ∧ (∃ T : Over S, Nonempty (Q.obj.obj ≅ yoneda.obj T)) ∧ IsEtale p₁.hom.hom ∧ IsEtale p₂.hom.hom ∧ IsEtale zU.hom.hom ∧ IsEtale qR.hom.hom ∧ IsChartwiseEtale wX ∧ IsChartwiseEtale c ∧ IsJointlySurjective (fun _ : Unit ↦ c.hom.hom) ∧ (∃ (Xₓ Uₓ Rₓ Wₓ Zₓ Qₓ : X.EnlargedEtaleSite) (p₁ₓ p₂ₓ : Rₓ ⟶ Uₓ) (zUₓ : Zₓ ⟶ Uₓ) (qRₓ : Qₓ ⟶ Rₓ) (cₓ : Zₓ ⟶ Wₓ) (q₁ₓ q₂ₓ : Qₓ ⟶ Zₓ) (wXₓ : Wₓ ⟶ Xₓ), Xₓ.obj = Over.mk (𝟙 X) ∧ Uₓ.obj = Over.mk p ∧ Rₓ.obj = Over.mk (p₁ ≫ p) ∧ Wₓ.obj = Over.mk wX ∧ Zₓ.obj = Over.mk (zU ≫ p) ∧ Qₓ.obj = Over.mk (qR ≫ p₁ ≫ p) ∧ HEq p₁ₓ.hom.left p₁ ∧ HEq p₂ₓ.hom.left p₂ ∧ HEq zUₓ.hom.left zU ∧ HEq qRₓ.hom.left qR ∧ HEq cₓ.hom.left c ∧ HEq q₁ₓ.hom.left q₁ ∧ HEq q₂ₓ.hom.left q₂ ∧ HEq wXₓ.hom.left wX ∧ Presieve.ofArrows (fun _ : Unit ↦ Zₓ) (fun _ : Unit ↦ cₓ) ∈ X.enlargedEtalePrecoverage Wₓ) ∧ (∃ e : Limits.pullback c.hom c.hom ≅ Q.obj, e.hom ≫ q₁.hom = Limits.pullback.fst c.hom c.hom ∧ e.hom ≫ q₂.hom = Limits.pullback.snd c.hom c.hom)
lean.note: The two declarations jointly state all clauses. Fibre products and their induced maps are given by limiting cones and their projection equations, so the statement is independent of the chosen fibre products. The first declaration includes representability by schemes, etaleness, an actual singleton covering in the enlarged site, and the overlap isomorphism characterized by both projections. The second states naturality under every map of etale test schemes. Both projection equations fix each comparison map uniquely; no arbitrary comparison map or extra geometric hypothesis is assumed.
